title: Lot: bring your household out of Sodom
reasons: At dawn the angels renew the 19:12 order: take your wife and daughters and depart; same speakers, occasion and direction.

title: Lot: flee to the permitted place of refuge
reasons: Angel's grant renews C0041's order; title 'permitted place of refuge' fits; note Zoar replaces the mountain. Lot's request stays in torah-genesis-19-12.

title: Ephron offers Abraham the field and cave
reasons: Ephron renews his offer in the same negotiation, naming the price and repeating 'Bury your dead'; the title still fits.

title: The servant recounts his prayer for a sign at the well
reasons: 24:43 ends mid-sentence; 24:44 completes the same recounted sign, same speaker and occasion, without changing the record.

title: Abimelech’s party seeks a covenant with Isaac
reasons: 26:28 breaks off mid-quotation; 26:29 states the sworn term the party seeks: 'that you shall do us no harm'.

title: Esau cries out for a blessing of his own
reasons: Only 27:38 repeats Esau's plea 'Bless me also, father'; 27:35–37 are Isaac's replies and Esau's complaint, so they are split off.

title: Joseph sends his steward after his brothers
reasons: 44:4 breaks off mid-message; 44:5 completes the words Joseph gives the steward to say about the silver cup.

title: Judah recalls Joseph asking to see Benjamin
reasons: Judah continues the same recollection of Joseph's demand that Benjamin come down; same speaker and occasion as 44:21; wording matches 43:3–5.

title: Pharaoh orders the brickmakers to gather their own straw
reasons: Speech formula reporting Pharaoh's command and naming its addressees, taskmasters and scribes; it opens 5:7 as 5:10 opens 5:11.

title: Jethro advises Moses to represent the people before God
reasons: Opening of Jethro's same counsel: his reason leads into 18:19's 'Now therefore listen to me'; same speaker and occasion, meaning unchanged.

title: Make the bronze-covered altar with horns, grating and rings
reasons: Continues the altar instruction (make it hollow, of boards, as shown on the mountain); C0277 stays itemized at 27:1–5, 8.

title: Priest: inspect and classify the affected garment or leather by the stated criteria
reasons: The re-inspection findings (unspread; unchanged after washing, so unclean) continue the same inspect-and-classify direction; C0496 stays at four verses.

title: The house owner: report a suspected house lesion to the priest
reasons: 14:34 is the protasis ('When you enter… and I put a lesion') of the same house-lesion law completed by 14:35.

title: Do not offer blemished or mutilated animals, including those supplied by foreigners
reasons: Opening of the same blemish law: offerers, resident foreigners included, must bring unblemished males; C0675 becomes 22:18–25, eight verses.

title: The priest's role when a husband suspects his wife
reasons: Closing ruling of the same jealousy law: the husband is free of guilt and the wife bears her sin; same speaker and law.

title: Nazirite: do not incur corpse defilement, even for close relatives
reasons: 6:8 closes the corpse-defilement rule (6:6–8), restating its ground: the Nazirite is holy to the Lord all his vowed days.

title: Moses asks Hobab to stay with Israel in the wilderness
reasons: Moses completes the same appeal to Hobab with its promise: 'if you go with us… we will do you good'.

title: Joshua and Caleb urge Israel to trust God
reasons: Same speech: the premise 'He will bring us into this land' leads straight into 14:9's 'Only do not become deserters'; meaning unchanged.

title: Israel: do not launch the presumptuous ascent after God's refusal
reasons: Moses' same warning continues: Amalek and the Canaanites are there and the Lord will not be among you; it completes 14:42's grounds.

title: God entrusts the sacred contributions to Aaron and his line
reasons: 18:19 renews the 18:8 grant in summary, adding daughters and the covenant of salt; same speaker, occasion and direction.

title: Set apart the best portion of the gifts due to God
reasons: Sanction of the same requirement: no sin once the best portion is set apart; do not profane the holy things, lest you die.

title: Reuben and Gad: cross armed with Israel before returning to your eastern possession
reasons: Negative sanction completing the same terms Moses sets in 32:20–22: if not, 'you shall sin before the Lord'.

title: The blood-avenger: execute the condemned murderer under the prescribed judgment
reasons: 35:21 ends by repeating C0945's clause verbatim (the avenger shall kill the murderer when he meets him); its enmity case stays with AUD-04-35-16.

title: Israel: depart Horeb for the commanded journey toward Canaan
reasons: 1:8 completes God's Horeb command of 1:6–7 (same speaker and occasion): 'Enter and inherit the land'; extend C0955 rather than link C0652.

title: Station the specified tribes on Gerizim and Ebal for the covenant ceremony
reasons: Speech formula reporting Moses' command that same day; it introduces the station order of 27:12–14 without changing it.

title: Moses tells the Levites to place the law beside the ark
reasons: Speech formula reporting Moses' command and naming its addressees, the Levites who carry the ark; it opens 31:26.

title: Joshua reminds the eastern tribes to cross armed with their brothers
reasons: 1:14 ends mid-sentence; 1:15 completes the same charge with its time limit and the return to the eastern inheritance.

title: The eastern tribes pledge obedience and encourage Joshua
reasons: The pledge of obedience named in the title begins at 1:16; same speakers and reply, with 1:17's wish inside it.

title: Rahab asks the spies to spare her household
reasons: After the spies' pledge, Rahab renews her request: 'you shall show me mercy and faithfulness'; same speaker and exchange.

title: The spies tell Rahab to mark her window with scarlet cord
reasons: The spies' same instructions continue with the oath's terms: keep everyone inside the house and do not disclose the agreement.

title: Joshua tells the tribal representatives to carry one stone each
reasons: Joshua's summons of the twelve tribal men opens the charge recorded at 4:5 ('summoned... and said to them'); same speaker and occasion.

title: The Lord tells Joshua to consecrate Israel and remove what was banned
reasons: Same divine speech: 'unless you remove that which is under the ban' states the direction that 7:13 repeats; meaning unchanged.

title: Joshua positions troops in ambush behind Ai
reasons: Joshua selects and sends the thirty thousand by night, the dispatch that 8:4's 'He commanded them' completes, as Numbers 22:5 opens 22:6.

title: Israel’s leaders assign the spared Gibeonites to cut wood and carry water
reasons: That day Joshua formally appoints them woodcutters and water-carriers, for the congregation and God's altar (cf. 9:23); same assignment and occasion.
Joshua formally appoints the Gibeonites woodcutters and water-carriers that day: the assignment of 9:21–23, same speaker and occasion.

title: Achsah asks Caleb for springs to accompany her land
reasons: Same exchange: Achsah's stated intent to ask for a field and Caleb's 'What is it?' prompt the request answered in 15:19.

title: Joshua tells the surveyors to divide the land into seven portions
reasons: Same instruction to the surveyors: Judah marks its boundary on the southwest and Joseph on the north while the land is divided.

title: Joshua urges Israel to take care to love the Lord
reasons: The “For if…” warning grounds the charge of 23:11 in the same speech (clinging to and intermarrying with the remaining nations); not a separate command.

title: Serve the Lord and remove foreign gods
reasons: Joshua seals the same exhortation with covenant, written law and witness stone, renewing X004’s direction without distinct substantive law (cf. ruling on 2 Kings 11:17).

title: Achsah asks Caleb for water rights in the southern land
reasons: Opens the same request: urged by Othniel, Achsah voices the southern-land complaint repeated in 1:15. Othniel’s reported urging needs no separate record.

title: Deborah and Barak call Israel to bless the Lord
reasons: Same song and singers renew 5:2's call: 'bless the Lord!' (5:9) and riders and travellers called to make music (5:10–11).

title: The Lord recalls warning Israel against fearing Amorite gods
reasons: Opening of the same oracle: the prophet's 'Thus says the Lord' and prologue lead into 6:10's recalled command; meaning unchanged.

title: Gideon asks the messenger to wait for his offering
reasons: Gideon's same request opens at 6:17 ('give me a sign'); waiting while he brings his offering is how the sign is sought.

title: Micah offers the Levite wages to serve as his priest
reasons: 17:10 breaks off ('And the Levite went'); 17:11 completes it, and 17:12 narrates Micah installing him as priest, completing the commission.

title: The Danite scouts urge their tribe to attack Laish
reasons: 18:10 completes the scouts' same exhortation, ending the quotation: a spacious land that 'God has delivered into your hands'.

title: The woman’s father urges the Levite to stay until afternoon
reasons: The same fifth-day urging continues: 'Lodge here today also… tomorrow you may rise early'; same speaker, occasion and direction to stay.

title: Israel’s leaders tell the Benjaminites to seize wives at Shiloh
reasons: 21:22 completes the leaders' same instruction, ending the quotation with their promise to answer the fathers' complaints.

title: Naomi urges her daughters-in-law to return home because she has no sons
reasons: 1:12 ends mid-sentence; 1:13 completes Naomi's same appeal ('No, my daughters'); 1:15 is already linked separately.

title: Naomi prepares Ruth to approach Boaz at the threshing floor
reasons: Opening of Naomi's same speech (seeking Ruth's rest; Boaz winnows tonight) leading into 3:3's instructions; same speaker, meaning unchanged.

title: Boaz asks Ruth to stay overnight and promises to act if the nearer kinsman declines
reasons: Boaz's same reply: 'do not be afraid', his promise, and the nearer kinsman to whom 3:13's 'if he will act' refers.

title: Elkanah tells Hannah to stay until Samuel is weaned
reasons: Hannah's proposal is what Elkanah's reply approves ('what has come from your mouth'); same exchange, as 1 Samuel 26:8 was added.

title: Eli rebukes his sons for their misconduct
reasons: Completes Eli’s rebuke in the same speech; the saying grounds his “Do not act this way.” Not a separate wisdom record.
Eli's rebuke opens at 2:23 ('Why do you act according to this report…?'); same speech, addressees and occasion.

title: The Philistine rulers send the ark from Ashdod to Gath
reasons: Ashdod's resolution, 'The ark… must not stay with us', is the same direction that convenes the rulers and moves the ark.

title: Israel asks Samuel for a king to judge them
reasons: Same speakers on the same occasion renew the demand for a king after Samuel's warning, so extend rather than parallel.
The people renew the 8:5 demand for a king at the same assembly (8:4–22), so extend; 8:19 begins the sentence.

title: Saul suggests going home and his servant proposes consulting a seer
reasons: The same exchange continues the servant's proposal (what to bring; 'You will give it to the man of God'), filling the gap before 9:9–10.

title: Samuel invites Saul to eat with him at the high place
reasons: Samuel's same reply continues: 'do not set your heart on' the donkeys, already found; same speaker, addressee and occasion.

title: Samuel has Israel assemble before the Lord by tribe and clan
reasons: Samuel's summons to Mizpah and 'Thus says the Lord' open the same address that ends in 10:19's order to stand by tribes.

title: Samuel asks Israel to witness the sign the Lord will give
reasons: Samuel's same call continues: the thunder sign is announced and 'Know and see that the evil you have done… is great'.

title: Samuel urges Israel to fear and serve the Lord sincerely
reasons: Same speech and charge (fear, serve and obey the Lord, people and king) stated conditionally; 12:24–25 restate it. Extend rather than duplicate.
Closing sanction of the same charge: if you do evil, you and your king 'will be added', that is, swept away.

title: Jonathan sets the condition for remaining in place
reasons: Opening of Jonathan's same plan ('We will cross to the men'), whose conditions follow in 14:9–10; speech formula and premise.

title: Saul gathers Israel’s chiefs to investigate the day’s offense
reasons: Saul's same speech binds the inquiry by oath: whoever is found guilty, even Jonathan, must die; it continues the direction.

title: Samuel relays the Lord’s order to strike Amalek
reasons: 15:2 opens the same oracle Samuel relays (‘Thus says the Lord Sabaoth’) and grounds the order; the origin basis already reads 15:2–3.

title: Samuel reminds Saul of his mission against Amalek
reasons: 15:17–19 form one rebuke: the anointing, the recalled mission, ‘why did you not listen?’ Same speaker and occasion; meaning unchanged.

title: Jonathan warns David to hide from Saul
reasons: 19:3 completes Jonathan’s same instruction (wait in the field; he will speak to Saul and report back); the quotation closes there.

title: Jonathan urges Saul not to wrong David
reasons: Extend only 19:5, which completes Jonathan’s plea; 19:6 is Saul’s compliance and oath, a response rather than the plea.

title: Saul orders David brought in on his bed to be killed
reasons: 19:14 reports Saul’s first sending to take David; 19:15 renews the same order after Michal’s excuse. Same occasion and direction.

title: Saul orders his guards to kill the priests and they refuse
reasons: Saul renews the same order to Doeg after the guards refuse: same speaker and occasion. Found by reviewer R8a; in no batch.

title: The medium urges Saul to eat before leaving
reasons: 28:23 reports the woman, now joined by the servants, renewing the same urging until Saul yields; same occasion, meaning unchanged.

title: David orders the Amalekite messenger struck down
reasons: The charge (1:14) and verdict (1:16) frame the same execution order, as AUD-10-4-9 keeps David’s charge with his order.

title: David demands that Michal be returned to him
reasons: Extend only 3:13, where David first demands Michal as the covenant’s condition; 3:15 is fulfilment narrative, not linked.

title: David orders Joab to expose Uriah to deadly fighting
reasons: 11:14 introduces the same letter (‘wrote a letter to Joab’), as ot-1-kings-v20-9 includes 20:8, where Jezebel writes hers.

title: Absalom demands that Joab arrange an audience with David
reasons: Extend only 14:29, the sendings 14:32 quotes; 14:30 is the separate barley order (ot-2-samuel-v14-30) and 14:31 Joab’s question.

title: David asks Hushai to return and counter Ahithophel’s advice
reasons: 15:33 is the first half of the same conditional (‘If you cross over… But if you return’), grounding the instruction.

title: David refuses to let his men stop Shimei’s curses
reasons: Abishai’s proposal is what David’s refusal answers; the catalogue keeps such proposals with refusals (1 Samuel 26:8–11; 2 Samuel 19:22–24).

title: Mephibosheth appeals to David after accusing his servant of slander
reasons: Opens the same appeal: Mephibosheth accuses his servant, quoting his order to saddle the donkey; the record’s title already describes this.

title: Barzillai asks to return home and sends Chimham in his place
reasons: 19:35–37 open Barzillai’s same reply: his age and declining the king’s offer ground the request to stay home.

title: David recounts God asking him to speak a parable about fearing God
reasons: 23:1–2 frame the same oracle (David’s last words; the Spirit speaking in him) that leads into the recounted charge; meaning unchanged.

title: Solomon has Adonijah brought from the altar and sends him home
reasons: Solomon’s conditional sparing of Adonijah is the ruling carried out in 1:53; same speaker and occasion, so extend rather than add.

title: David calls on Solomon to be strong as he faces death
reasons: 2:1 is the same charge’s narrative frame (‘he commanded his son Solomon, saying’), like published frames such as 2 Kings 22:12.

title: Solomon asks Hiram to have cedar timber cut in Lebanon
reasons: 5:16–19 open the same message to Hiram (frame, purpose, plan to build); the request is unchanged. 5:19 stays linked to ot-1-chronicles-v28-10.

title: Solomon recounts God appointing David’s son to build the temple
reasons: 8:18 begins the same quoted word of the Lord (‘you did well… Nevertheless, you shall not build’); one quotation, meaning unchanged.

title: Asa offers gifts for an alliance and asks Syria to break with Baasha
reasons: 15:18 sends the gifts by envoys, ‘saying’, introducing the same message; the gifts are those named in 15:19.

title: Elijah tells Ahab to gather Israel and the prophets at Carmel
reasons: 18:18 opens Elijah’s same reply; the rebuke grounds the ‘Now send and gather’ summons, as an indictment opens Ezra 10:10–11.

title: Orders concerning the district rulers’ attendants during the siege
reasons: Verified as asked: 21:18–19a is one speech of Syria's king to his men about Samaria's attendants coming out; same speaker, recipients, occasion.

title: Jehoshaphat challenges Ahab’s dismissal of Micaiah and Ahab summons him
reasons: Jehoshaphat’s request for a prophet of the Lord opens the exchange; the record’s parallel 2 Chronicles 18:6–8 already includes its counterpart, 18:6.
Jehoshaphat's request for a prophet of the Lord opens the recorded exchange; its Chronicles parallel 18:6 is already linked to this record.

title: Micaiah recounts a spirit being permitted to deceive Ahab’s prophets
reasons: 22:19–21 hold the vision and the Lord’s call, ‘Who will deceive Ahab?’, which the commission at 22:22 completes; one recounted scene.

title: Ahaziah sends messengers to inquire of Baal-zebub
reasons: 1:4 completes the message the angel charges Elijah to deliver (1:3), as the messengers repeat it in 1:6; same commission.

title: The prophets press Elisha to let them search for Elijah
reasons: Elisha expressly recalls his own prohibition (‘Did I not tell you, Do not go?’) at the close of the same episode.

title: Elisha calls for a musician and gives the Lord’s instruction to dig pits
reasons: Extend 3:17–18, the oracle’s promise explaining the pits; 3:19 predicts conquest and devastation, a different matter that would change the record.

title: The prophets ask Elisha to let them build by the Jordan
reasons: 6:1 opens the same request (the place is too narrow); 6:3 completes it, asking Elisha to come along. One exchange.

title: A woman recounts a desperate bargain made during the famine
reasons: 6:29 completes the woman’s same account and repeats the demand ‘Give your son’; her quotation closes there.

title: Four men with leprosy decide to risk entering the Syrian camp
reasons: 7:3 introduces the four men and opens the same deliberation (‘Why are we sitting here until we die?’), as 1 Maccabees 2:40–41.

title: The prophetic messenger anoints Jehu and charges him to avenge the slain prophets
reasons: 9:10 ends the same oracle with Jezebel’s fate (cf. ‘at Jezebel’s hand’, 9:7); the quotation closes there.

title: Jehu invites Jonadab to witness his zeal
reasons: ‘Give me your hand’ and seating Jonadab in the chariot begin the same invitation that 10:16 completes.

title: Jehu orders his men to kill the assembled worshipers of Baal
reasons: 10:24 posts the guards under the same no-escape order, on pain of life, that 10:25 repeats (‘Let no man come out’).

title: Israel is warned to remember the covenant and reject other gods
reasons: 17:39 is the positive half of the same charge: no other gods, ‘but you shall fear the Lord your God’.

title: The Assyrian envoy tells Jerusalem not to trust Hezekiah
reasons: 18:28’s summons, ‘Hear the words of the great king’, opens the same message; same speaker and occasion.

title: Hezekiah asks Isaiah to pray for the remnant
reasons: Hezekiah sends the delegation that carries the recorded message (19:3–4); the parallel Isaiah 37:2–4 record likewise includes the sending.

title: Sennacherib warns Hezekiah against trusting God to save Jerusalem
reasons: 19:9 sends the messengers ‘saying’, introducing the same warning; a frame like those in published extensions.

title: The Lord sends Isaiah back with a promise to heal Hezekiah
reasons: 20:6 completes the message Isaiah must deliver; 20:5 breaks off mid-sentence and the quotation closes at 20:6.

title: Huldah directs the officials to relay the Lord’s answer to Josiah
reasons: Extend only 22:18, the renewed ‘say this’ charge (as 2 Chronicles 34:26 is linked); 22:16–17 and 22:19–20 are the oracle’s predictions.

title: David tells the Levites to purify themselves and carry the ark
reasons: David's summons names the priests and Levite chiefs addressed in 15:12 ('He said to them'); same speaker, occasion and charge.

title: David’s song calls for thanksgiving and prayer for rescue
reasons: The people’s ‘Amen’ continues the song’s direction ‘Say…’ in 16:35; same speaker and occasion as ot-1-chronicles-v16-34, so no new Command.

title: David asks to purchase Orna’s threshing floor for an altar
reasons: David renews his demand to pay full price; the record’s parallel 2 Samuel 24:21–24 already includes the matching 24:24.

title: David urges Solomon to keep Moses’ ordinances and take courage
reasons: 22:11–12 open the same charge (‘He will grant success… to observe the law’), which 22:13 continues: ‘Then He will grant success, if…’.

title: Solomon asks Hiram for a skilled artisan and timber from Lebanon
reasons: One letter: 2:2–5 open it, 2:8 finishes 2:7’s broken sentence and 2:9 states the provisions; the request is unchanged.

title: Rehoboam’s young advisers tell him to answer the people harshly
reasons: 10:11 completes the advisers’ words (1 Kings 12:11 already linked); 10:9 is the request they answer, as AUD-11-12-6 keeps 12:6.

title: Asa asks Syria’s king to make an alliance and drive Baasha away
reasons: 16:2 sends the gold and silver ‘saying’, introducing the same message; same frame as 1 Kings 15:18.

title: Micaiah recounts a spirit being permitted to deceive the king’s prophets
reasons: The vision and the Lord’s call for a volunteer (18:18–20) open the same commission completed at 18:21; one recounted scene.

title: Joash orders a collection for annual temple repairs
reasons: After the Levites delay, Joash presses the same collection on Jehoiada, citing Moses’ levy; same speaker, occasion and direction.

title: Amaziah threatens the prophet who rebukes him
reasons: 25:15 is the rebuke the title names and 25:16 calls ‘my counsel’; the record already includes the prophet’s reply.

title: Amaziah challenges Joash, who answers with the thornbush story
reasons: Reconciled with Kings: ot-2-kings-v14-9 keeps the story with its application (14:9–10); 25:19 is that application in Joash's same reply.

title: Oded calls on Israel to send Judah’s captives back
reasons: 28:9–10 open Oded’s same address; the indictment grounds the release command, as Ezra 10:10 opens Ezra’s charge.

title: Hezekiah tells the Levites to purify themselves and the temple
reasons: 29:4 gathers and stations the priests and Levites addressed in 29:5, as 1 Maccabees 16:2 names those summoned; meaning unchanged.

title: Hezekiah urges his people not to fear the Assyrian army
reasons: Completes Hezekiah's speech (32:7–8), as reviewer R2a noted.

title: Judas orders his troops to prepare for battle at dawn
reasons: Same speech and occasion: Judas's quotation begun at 3:58 closes at 3:60; the 'better… than' line and trust in Heaven motivate the order.

title: Joseph and Azariah seek a name for themselves in battle
reasons: 5:58 reports their orders to the force, turning the same resolve into a command to march; same speakers and occasion.

title: The king’s side proposes peace and restoration of Jewish customs
reasons: Extend only 6:57, which opens Lysias’s same proposal; 6:60–61 narrate its adoption and sworn implementation, fulfilment narrative.

title: Alcimus urges Demetrius to investigate and punish Judas’s supporters
reasons: The accusation (7:6) opens the same appeal to the king; one quotation, same speakers and occasion.

title: Rome and Judea establish mutual treaty obligations
reasons: Close of the same Roman letter: the senate applies its pledge of help (8:27) by warning Demetrius; question and threat need no separate record.

title: Alexander asks for Ptolemy’s daughter in marriage
reasons: 10:51–53 are the same letter’s frame and opening, leading into the marriage request; meaning unchanged.

title: Ptolemy agrees to a marriage alliance and proposes a meeting
reasons: 10:55 opens Ptolemy’s same reply; one quotation, meaning unchanged.

title: Jonathan sends envoys to Rome and letters to Sparta to renew ties
reasons: The letter named in 12:2 restates the envoys' commission, charges them to Sparta and asks a reply; 12:3 (envoys' delivery in Rome) added too.

title: Tryphon deceives Jonathan into dismissing his troops
reasons: Same speaker and deception: the feigned honours and order to obey Jonathan (12:43) and the speech's opening question (12:44) belong to the 12:45 ploy.

title: Tryphon demands silver and hostages for Jonathan’s release
reasons: 13:14–15 send the envoys and state the debt pretext that opens the same demand; one message.

title: Demetrius II confirms Judea's strongholds and remits offenses and levies
reasons: Final clause of the same Demetrius II letter (the quotation closes at 13:40); enrollment and peace complete the charter.

title: Nehemiah sends priests’ descendants to recover the hidden fire
reasons: Same speaker and fire ritual: Nehemiah's further order for the remaining water continues 1:21; 1:32 is outcome narrative.
Nehemiah's further order in the same fire-recovery procedure, with the same liquid as 1:21; extend rather than a new record (cf. N:GAP-16-1-31).

title: Eleazar refuses to mislead younger people by pretending to break the law
reasons: Extend 6:18–20: they introduce ‘the man’ of 6:21 and the narrator’s maxim on refusing unlawful food; 6:29–31 narrate his death.

title: Judas urges his men to fight to the death for law and homeland
reasons: Judas’s council decision to go out and decide matters with God’s help leads straight into his recorded exhortation; same speaker and occasion.

title: Jewish companions urge Nicanor to honor the Sabbath
reasons: Asked who commanded it, the same companions renew their plea by citing the Lord’s command to keep the seventh day.

title: Judas urges his men to remember past help from heaven
reasons: Judas's same exhortation continues: he gives orders, exposes the nations' perjury and arms his men with encouraging words.

title: The king orders the rebuilding of Jerusalem to stop
reasons: Opening of the same royal letter whose stop order is recorded (4:21–22); extend, adding 4:20 to complete the sentence.

title: The king entrusts Ezra with offerings and funds for the temple
reasons: 7:15–16 name the silver, gold and freewill offerings entrusted in the same sentence that 7:17–20 assigns; 7:18 presupposes them.

title: Shecaniah proposes an oath to send away foreign wives and their children
reasons: 10:2 opens Shecaniah’s same proposal with confession and hope, as the published Ezra 10:10–11 keeps its indictment.

title: The assembly proposes scheduled hearings for foreign marriages
reasons: 10:12–13 open the assembly’s same reply, giving the reasons for the proposed schedule; one quotation.

title: Nehemiah has the lenders swear to return what they took
reasons: Nehemiah seals the same oath with a curse on whoever fails to uphold ‘this word’; the assembly’s Amen completes the ceremony.

title: Sanballat uses an accusation to press Nehemiah for a meeting
reasons: 6:5–6 send the open letter and begin its accusation; 6:7 continues the same letter.

title: Nehemiah shuts Jerusalem’s gates against Sabbath trade
reasons: 13:15–18 report Nehemiah’s warning to Sabbath sellers and rebuke of Judah’s nobles, the same campaign against Sabbath trade.

title: The advisers propose removing Vashti by royal decree
reasons: 1:16–18 open Muchaeus’s same speech, giving the grounds for the proposed decree; one quotation.

title: Esther sends her reply to Mordecai through a messenger
reasons: 4:10 stops at ‘say:’; 4:11 is the reply itself, citing the court law. Extend rather than present Esther’s report as a royal law.

title: Blessed is the one who considers the poor and needy
reasons: 40:3–4 complete the beatitude: the Lord’s promised protection of the one who considers the poor, which the record’s own note cites.

title: The psalmist tells his own soul to submit to God as his hope
reasons: First occurrence of the refrain recorded at 61:6–8, as the record's note says; same psalm and speaker. 61:2 included to keep the refrain whole.

title: The nations allied against Israel plot to wipe out its name
reasons: The same coalition rulers’ plot quoted again (‘Let us inherit God’s sanctuary’), as the record’s note says; same speakers and occasion.

title: Keep away from the seducer's house
reasons: 5:11 continues the sentence of 5:8–10: the regret that follows ignoring the warning. Same speaker and charge, not a separate direction.

title: Stolen water tastes sweet, but Folly's guests perish
reasons: Folly's call ('turn aside to me') runs straight into her words at 9:17; join it to AUD-22-9-17, mirroring Wisdom's invitation 9:1–6.
Folly's call opens the speech continued in 9:17; extend the Folly record (as Wisdom's 9:1–6) rather than make a separate record.

title: Give your parents reason to rejoice
reasons: 23:27 ('for…') completes 23:26's sentence: keep my ways, for another's house is a leaking jar. Motive of the same charge, so extend.

title: A mother counsels the king about wine and sound judgment
reasons: Heading and opening appeal of the same mother's instruction; 'keep God's sayings' comes as a question, so extend rather than create.

title: Nothing is new under the sun, and the past is forgotten
reasons: The cycles of generations, sun, wind and streams are the premise of ‘all things are wearisome… nothing new’ (1:8–11); same speaker and poem.

title: Do not be surprised by oppression under layers of officials
reasons: 5:8 completes 5:7's reasoning about officials over officials, ending with the king and the land's yield. Same saying, not a new direction.

title: The lament asks passersby to witness its incomparable sorrow
reasons: Zion renews the same appeal (‘Hear… all you peoples, and see my pain’) in the same lament; attach to that Study Context record.

title: The lament calls the people to return to the Lord
reasons: 3:39's question (why grumble over one's sin?) leads straight into 'let us return'; same speaker and sense unit, not a separate direction.

title: Blessed are the undefiled barren woman and the faithful eunuch
reasons: 3:16 ('But…') is the antithesis of 3:13's beatitude: undefiled bed versus unlawful bed. Completes the same teaching rather than a separate record.

title: Childlessness with virtue is better, for virtue is remembered
reasons: 4:3 ('But…') completes 4:1–2's 'better' saying: virtuous childlessness against the rootless offspring of the ungodly. Same teaching, so extend.

title: Do not imagine you can hide from God
reasons: 16:18–19 answer 16:17's quoted thought: heaven and earth shake when He looks on them, so none can hide. Same speaker, continuing passage.

title: Do not repeat what was said in confidence
reasons: 19:5 opens the sentence that 19:6 completes ('…but the one who hates chatter'); 19:9 is already in the record, so add only 19:5.

title: A wife's adultery breaks God's law and wrongs her husband
reasons: Same adulteress as 23:22–23: her public judgment, rootless children and cursed memory complete the passage. Extending avoids a duplicate record.

title: A gracious, silent and modest wife is a gift of the Lord
reasons: Continues 26:13–15's praise of a good wife (her beauty in an ordered house) with the same speaker; not a separate direction.

title: Take comfort and do not let grief consume you
reasons: 30:24 is already in the record; 30:25 closes the same saying on a glad heart that cares for its food.

title: A banquet leader should serve without exalting himself
reasons: The similes give the reason behind 32:3–4's 'do not hinder the music'; same banquet counsel and speaker.

title: Speak briefly when you are asked to speak
reasons: 32:10 gives the motive for 32:9's modesty: grace goes ahead of a modest person. Same counsel.

title: Human beings are like clay in the hand of their Maker
reasons: First half of the same comparison: as the Lord distinguished days, so people (33:8 and 33:11 match). Doctrine alone; extend, not a record.

title: God's mercy in affliction is like rain in drought
reasons: 35:19–23 is one sentence; AUD-27-35-23 now starts mid-sentence at 'until He judges'. Extend back to 35:19 and broaden its title.

title: Seek counsel from someone godly who shares your concerns
reasons: 37:14 ('For…') is the reason for 37:13's counsel to trust your own heart; same saying.

title: Do not reject the medicines the Lord created from the earth
reasons: Continues 38:4–5 on medicines: God gave the knowledge by which He heals. Repeats existing coverage, so extend rather than a new record.

title: A scribe’s study takes leisure that farm labor leaves little room for
reasons: Craftsman, smith and potter continue the list begun with the farmer in 38:25–26 ('So also…'); part of the scribe-and-trades comparison.

title: God's ways bless the holy but trip up the lawless
reasons: 39:26–27 continue 39:25 in AUD-27-39-22: life's necessities are good for the godly but turn evil for sinners. Same teaching.
Continues the same strophe (39:25 'evil things for sinners'): forces of retribution created to serve His command. Extend; not a separate teaching.

title: Toil and fear of death burden everyone, from throne to ashes
reasons: Continues 40:1–4's burden on all mortals: even sleep brings anxious dreams. Same passage and teaching.

title: Remember others who have died and do not fear death
reasons: Opens the same saying on death: 41:3 takes up 41:2's 'sentence' ('Do not fear death's sentence'). Same speaker and passage.

title: Sirach's advice to fathers about a daughter's reputation
reasons: 42:9–10 are already in the record; 42:13–14 ('For…') give the reason for 42:12's direction, so add only those.

title: Isaiah is to reassure Ahaz about the two threatening kings
reasons: Body of the message Isaiah must deliver (7:4–9; 7:9 already linked): the plot is quoted only to be annulled. Not a separate plan record.

title: The Lord tells Isaiah to write the warning for future generations
reasons: 'Announce to them' is the same charge to Isaiah that 30:8 continues ('Now then… write these things'). Same speaker and occasion.

title: Under righteous rule fools will no longer be called to govern
reasons: 32:6 ('For…') explains 32:5: the fool's lawless counsel against the devout's lasting plans. Continues that record; no separate direction.

title: The Assyrian envoy challenges Hezekiah’s confidence
reasons: 36:5–10 completes the message Rapsakes tells the officials to deliver (36:4), including the horse wager (36:8) and claimed divine sanction (36:10).

title: A wilderness voice calls for preparing the Lord’s way
reasons: Continues the same voice's call to prepare the way (levelling the road); Luke 3:5, already linked to this record, quotes it.

title: Israel is challenged over its claim that God does not see its plight
reasons: The answer to Israel’s complaint in the same address: the unwearied God strengthens those who endure for Him. Completes the record’s passage.

title: Desert settlements and Petra are called to rejoice
reasons: Completes the call of 42:11: Kedar's and Petra's people give God glory and announce His praise. Same hymn; 42:8 shares only vocabulary.

title: God calls Jacob and Israel to remember their Maker
reasons: ‘Know… see’ closes the idol satire with the lesson that 44:21’s ‘Remember these things’ refers to; the same appeal to Israel.

title: Survivors from the nations are called to gather, unlike idol worshippers
reasons: 45:21 continues the summons ('let them draw near so that they may know together'); same speaker and occasion.

title: The fast God chooses releases people from injustice and coercion
reasons: Negative half of the same instruction: 'I did not choose this fast' (58:5) leads into 58:6's 'It is not such a fast.' Extend.

title: Judah is warned against trusting in slogans about the temple
reasons: 7:8 restates 7:4's warning against trusting false words; the sentence runs to 7:11's 'robbers' cave'. Same sermon and direction.

title: God recalls telling Israel to listen and walk in His ways
reasons: 7:22–23 is one sentence: God did not command sacrifice but ‘Hear My voice’. 7:22 is the contrast half of the recorded recollection.

title: A prayer acknowledges the Lord’s declaration against Babylon
reasons: 28:61 opens Jeremiah's charge to Seraiah that 28:62 continues ('and say'); consider retitling as that charge.

title: God gives Jeremiah the cup of judgment to take to the nations
reasons: Completes the 32:15 sentence: give the cup to the nations, and they will drink and go mad. Same speaker and occasion.

title: The cup pictures nations falling under the sword of judgment
reasons: Continues the same instruction to Jeremiah: if the nations refuse the cup, say 'You will certainly drink.'

title: God tells the exiles that He did not send Shemaiah to prophesy
reasons: Word-event formula that directly introduces the recorded order 'Send to the deportees' (36:31); the catalogue adds such introductions (cf. 2 Kings 22:3).

title: The Rechabites recount Jonadab’s rule on houses, crops and tents
reasons: Closing sentence of the same Rechabite reply: why, despite the tent rule, they now live in Jerusalem. Same speakers and occasion.

title: God sends Jeremiah to ask why Judah refuses instruction
reasons: 42:14 is the content of the message 42:13 sends Jeremiah to deliver: the Rechabites obeyed, Judah did not listen.

title: God tells Jeremiah to hide stones at Pharaoh’s gate in Tahpanhes
reasons: Word-event formula directly introducing the recorded order to hide stones at Taphnas (50:9); same speaker and occasion.

title: God tells Ezekiel to listen and eat what he is given
reasons: 3:1 and 3:3 renew 2:8's command to eat; 2:9–10 and 3:2 are the connecting vision and fulfilment within the same passage.

title: God appoints Ezekiel as a watchman to warn Israel
reasons: Word-event formula directly introducing the recorded watchman appointment (3:17); same speaker and occasion.

title: Ezekiel identifies Jerusalem’s ruler in the sign of deportation
reasons: Formula and the Lord's question introduce the recorded 'Say to them' (12:10); same speaker. 12:9 is included to keep the speech contiguous.

title: Ezekiel is told to wail because the sword has come on Israel
reasons: 21:19 renews the sign ('strike hand upon hand'); extended to 21:20 because the sentence ends there. Reference corrected from 21:18–19.

title: God says He will profane the sanctuary Israel takes pride in
reasons: Ezekiel's word-event formula introducing the message he is told to relay (24:21); same speaker and occasion.

title: The oracle summons birds and beasts to a feast after judgment
reasons: 39:18–20 continue the same summons to birds and beasts ('you will eat… drink'); same speaker and occasion.

title: God promises to dwell with Israel when they put away idolatry and bloodshed
reasons: 43:7–9 is one speech: Israel will no longer profane My name by prostitution and murder; 43:9 turns it into the direction.

title: Nebuchadnezzar demands that the Chaldeans tell and interpret his dream
reasons: 2:2 is the reported summons to report the dream and 2:8–9 the renewed demand: same king, occasion and direction, as the record’s note says.

title: The Lord teaches Jonah to share His compassion for Nineveh
reasons: The Lord's first teaching question about Jonah's anger over Nineveh; 4:9 repeats it. Same speaker and occasion; the gourd narrative is not added.

title: Zechariah announces the one called Rising who will build the Lord’s house
reasons: Rest of the message Zechariah is told to speak (6:12–15), ending with its condition: ‘if you truly listen to the voice of the Lord’.

title: Jesus sends the man he healed to the priest with the prescribed offering
reasons: Same occasion: the healing word 'be cleansed' precedes the charge; matches the linked Mark 1:40–45 and pericope practice (Luke 17:11–19).

title: The chief priests decline to put blood money in the treasury
reasons: Immediate occasion: Judas returns the silver confessing ‘innocent blood’ and throws it into the sanctuary, prompting the priests’ blood-price ruling (27:6).

title: Jesus calls the temple a house of prayer for all nations
reasons: Same Markan pericope as K023 (11:17): the expulsion and the ban on carrying vessels that the house-of-prayer saying explains; Luke 19:45–46 is linked there.

title: Hear God’s word and do it
reasons: Immediate occasion: the report that his mother and brothers stand outside prompts 8:21; the linked Matthew 12:46–50 and Mark 3:31–35 already include it.

title: Trust Jesus and care for the restored child
reasons: Immediate occasion: ‘Do not trouble the Teacher any longer’ is what ‘Do not fear; only believe’ answers; the linked Mark 5:35–43 includes it.

title: Remember Lot’s wife and do not turn back
reasons: Same speech and warning: one taken, one left closes the charge not to turn back (17:31–33), whose antecedent 17:26–31 is already linked.

title: Jesus teaches Nicodemus about birth from above
reasons: Same speech to Nicodemus (the quotation runs to 3:21); 3:16 restates 3:15 inside K032, so extend K032 rather than parallel K031.

title: Jesus sends his disciples to reap where others have labored
reasons: Same exchange with the disciples: their ‘Rabbi, eat’ and Jesus’ food of doing the Sender’s will lead straight into the harvest commission (4:35).

title: Honor the Son as the Father is honored
reasons: 5:17 opens the discourse AUD-47-5-19 continues (‘So Jesus answered them’, 5:19): the Son works as the Father works. 5:16, 18 give occasion and reaction.

title: The authorities threaten synagogue exclusion for confessing Jesus as Christ
reasons: Same authorities and hearing: ‘Give glory to God’ (9:24) renews the pressure behind 9:22; 9:25–34 is testimony and plain fulfilment.

title: Jesus’ accusers invoke their law in demanding his death
reasons: The accusers renew their demand (‘not Caesar’s friend’, 19:12; ‘Crucify Him!’, 19:15). 19:8–11 is Pilate’s separate exchange with Jesus, not added.
The same accusers renew the demand 'Crucify Him!' before Pilate in the same trial; extend this verse, not all of 19:8–15.

title: Peter connects the outpouring of the Spirit with Joel’s prophecy
reasons: Same speech: Peter’s call to listen (2:14) and ‘not drunk’ (2:15) run straight into ‘Rather, this is what was spoken’ (2:16).

title: Salvation is found in Jesus alone
reasons: Same short speech: healing ‘in the name of Jesus Christ’ and the rejected stone (4:10–11) lead directly into ‘no other name’ (4:12).

title: The risen Jesus appoints Paul as a servant and witness
reasons: Same speech and occasion: the light and Jesus' opening words lead straight into 26:15–18; they lack the Damascus order, so AUD-48-9-3 does not fit.

title: Do not boast over the branches; remain in God’s kindness
reasons: Same speech: Paul discloses the mystery ‘so that you may not be wise in your own eyes’, renewing the warning against boasting.

title: Imitate Paul’s example and hear Timothy’s reminder
reasons: 4:9–13 is the apostolic conduct ‘these things’ (4:14) describe and 4:16 asks them to imitate; 4:18–21 closes the same fatherly admonition.

title: Look to what is unseen and lasting amid affliction
reasons: 4:7–15 grounds ‘Therefore we do not lose heart’ (4:16); 5:1–8 continues the same contrast of seen and unseen across the chapter break.
5:1–8 continues 4:16–18 across the chapter break: the eternal unseen dwelling and ‘we walk by faith, not by sight’ (5:7).

title: Examine yourselves and seek restoration and peace
reasons: Paul’s warning (‘I will not spare’) is his own plan, not a standalone direction; it leads into 13:5’s self-examination (cf. 13:10). 13:1 is A085.

title: Stand firm in freedom rather than seeking justification through circumcision
reasons: 5:7–12 continues 5:1–6 against the circumcision agitators (‘the one troubling you will bear the judgment’). 4:13–20 is Paul’s personal appeal; not added.

title: Proclaim Christ’s riches among the nations
reasons: Same commission: ‘the stewardship of God’s grace that was given to me for you’ (3:2) and the mystery it proclaims (3:3–6) lead into 3:7.

title: Husbands are called to love their wives as Christ loved the church
reasons: 5:26–27 completes the 5:25 sentence: Christ gave himself to sanctify the church, the husbands’ pattern. 5:31–33 is already linked to A049.

title: Press on and follow faithful examples
reasons: Paul’s example of counting all loss runs into 3:12 (‘Not that I have already obtained it’); 3:15–17 tells readers to imitate it.

title: Continue diligent service and imitate those who inherit the promises
reasons: ‘For’ (6:13): Abraham, who ‘waited patiently’ and obtained the promise, illustrates 6:12, and 6:18 renews ‘hold fast the hope’; one argument to 6:20.

title: Abel, Enoch, and Noah as examples of faith
reasons: The definition of faith heads the examples A072 begins at 11:4; 11:6, already in A072, depends on it. Same speaker and passage.

title: Heed the One who speaks and worship with gratitude and reverence
reasons: The Sinai–Zion contrast grounds ‘See that you do not refuse the One who speaks’ (12:25) and its earth–heaven comparison; 12:20 stays linked to C0140.

title: Remember, repent and return to the first works
reasons: 2:2–3 is already in X009; add the letter’s opening ‘write’ (2:1), as X011 and AUD-70-2-12 to AUD-70-3-14 include theirs.

title: Remain faithful through suffering
reasons: 2:9 is already in X010; add the letter’s opening ‘write’ (2:8), as X011 and AUD-70-2-12 to AUD-70-3-14 include theirs.
